They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## Expression Contexts 435 436 Expressions behave differently depending on where they appear. 437 438 ### Script Node Body 439 440 The `inputs.script` field contains a function body. Full JavaScript statements are allowed (variables, loops, conditionals). The returned value becomes `$vars.{nodeId}.output`. 441 442 Scripts can return any value — objects, numbers, strings, arrays, or booleans: 443 444 ```javascript 445 // Returning an object (multiple fields) 446 const items = $vars.fetchData.output.body.items; 447 const filtered = items.filter(i => i.active); 448 return { count: filtered.length, names: filtered.map(i => i.name) }; 449 450 // Returning a bare value (useful for accumulators in loops) 451 return $vars.total + $vars.loop1.currentItem; 452 ``` 453 454 ### Decision Node (`inputs.expression`) 455 456 A single boolean expression. Result is coerced to `Boolean()`. 457 458 ``` 459 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.verified === true 460 ``` 461 462 Determines which port fires: `true` or `false`. 463 464 ### Switch Node (`inputs.cases[].expression`) 465 466 Each case has an expression evaluated in order. First truthy result wins; otherwise the `default` port fires. 467 468 ```json 469 { 470 "inputs": { 471 "cases": [ 472 { "label": "Low", "expression": "$vars.score <= 30" }, 473 { "label": "Medium", "expression": "$vars.score <= 70" }, 474 { "label": "High", "expression": "$vars.score > 70" } 475 ] 476 } 477 } 478 ``` 479 480 ### HTTP Branch Condition (`inputs.branches[].conditionExpression`) 481 482 Uses `$self` to reference the current HTTP node's response. 483 484 ``` 485 $self.output.statusCode >= 200 && $self.output.statusCode < 300 486 ``` 487 488 ### Variable Update Expressions 489 490 Evaluate to the new value for the target variable. 491 492 ``` 493 =js:$vars.counter + 1 494 =js:$vars.items.concat([$vars.newItem.output]) 495 ``` 496 497 ### Loop Collection Expression 498 499 The `inputs.collection` field on a Loop node resolves to an array to iterate over. 500 501 ``` 502 =js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items 503 =js:$vars.inputArray.filter(x => x.active) 504 ``` 505 506 Inside the loop body, use `$vars..currentItem` and `$vars..currentIndex` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 507 508 --- 509 510 ## Jint Engine Constraints 511 512 The production runtime uses **Jint** (a .NET JavaScript interpreter, ES2020 subset). Key constraints: 513 514 ### Supported 515 516 - Arithmetic: `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%` 517 - Comparison: `===`, `!==`, `==`, `!=`, `>`, `<`, `>=`, `<=` 518 - Logical: `&&`, `||`, `!` 519 - Ternary: `condition ? a : b` 520 - String methods: `.toUpperCase()`, `.toLowerCase()`, `.trim()`, `.split()`, `.includes()`, `.startsWith()`, `.slice()`, `.substring()` 521 - Array methods: `.filter()`, `.map()`, `.reduce()`, `.find()`, `.some()`, `.every()`, `.concat()`, `.length` 522 - Object: `Object.keys()`, `Object.values()`, `Object.entries()` 523 - Math: `Math.floor()`, `Math.ceil()`, `Math.round()`, `Math.abs()`, `Math.min()`, `Math.max()`, `Math.random()` 524 - JSON: `JSON.parse()`, `JSON.stringify()` 525 - Template literals: `` `Hello ${name}` `` 526 - Destructuring: `const { a, b } = obj` (in script bodies) 527 - Spread operator: `[...arr1, ...arr2]` (in script bodies) 528 - Arrow functions: `items.filter(x => x.active)` (inline callbacks) 529 530 ### Not Supported 531 532 - `fetch`, `XMLHttpRequest`, `setTimeout`, `setInterval` — no network or timers 533 - `document`, `window`, `console` — no DOM or browser globals 534 - `require`, `import` — no module system 535 - `eval`, `Function` constructor — no dynamic code generation 536 - `async`/`await`, `Promise` — no async operations 537 - `Date` constructor may have limited support — prefer ISO 8601 strings 538 539 > **When in doubt, keep expressions simple.** Complex data processing should go in Script nodes where you have full statement support, not in one-line expressions. 540 541 --- 542 543 ## Scoping Rules 544 545 ### Node Output Availability 546 547 A node's output (`$vars.{nodeId}.output`) is available to **all downstream nodes** connected via edges. If a node has not executed (e.g., on an untaken branch), its `$vars` entry is `undefined`. 548 549 ### Loop Scope 550 551 Inside a loop body, you have access to: 552 - All parent-scope `$vars` (read-only from loop's perspective) 553 - `$vars..currentItem` — current array element 554 - `$vars..currentIndex` — zero-based index 555 - `$vars..collection` — the original array 556 557 Where `` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`). 558 559 > **Important:** Loop body nodes must have `"parentId": ""` set in their JSON. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is inside the loop and `$vars..currentItem` will be undefined. 560 561 After loop completion, `$vars..output` contains aggregated results from all iterations. 562 563 ### Subflow Scope 564 565 Subflows have their own variable scope. Parent variables are **not** automatically visible inside a subflow. Pass values explicitly via subflow `inputs` and receive results via subflow `outputs`. 566 567 --- 568 569 ## Variable Management via CLI 570 571 There are **no CLI commands** for adding or removing variables. Manage variables with `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 572 573 ### Adding a workflow input variable 574 575 1. Open `.flow` 576 2. Add the variable object to `variables.globals` 577 3. Run `uip maestro flow validate` to check for errors 578 579 ### Adding node variables after manual node insertion 580 581 When adding nodes via `Edit` (not CLI), you must also add corresponding entries to `variables.nodes`: 582 583 ```json 584 { 585 "id": "myScript.output", 586 "type": "object", 587 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "output" } 588 }, 589 { 590 "id": "myScript.error", 591 "type": "object", 592 "binding": { "nodeId": "myScript", "outputId": "error" } 593 } 594 ``` 595 596 > **When using `uip maestro flow node add`**, node variables are handled automatically. Only add them manually when using `Edit` against the `.flow` file. 597 598 ### Mapping outputs on End nodes 599 600 For every `out` variable, add a mapping in each End node's `outputs`: 601 602 ```json 603 "outputs": { 604 "result": { 605 "source": "=js:$vars.processData.output" 606 } 607 } 608 ``` 609 610 --- 611 612 ## Complete Example 613 614 A flow with input, state, and output 21	## Top-level structure
22	
23	```json
24	{
25	  "id": "<uuid>",
26	  "version": "<version from `uip maestro flow init`>",
27	  "name": "MyFlow",
28	  "nodes": [],
29	  "edges": [],
30	  "definitions": [],
31	  "bindings": [],

33	  "layout": {

35	  }
36	}

38	
39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." See [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](../author/references/greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
40	
41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.
42	
43	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.
44	
45	> **Don't confuse top-level `version` with `definitions[].version` / `typeVersion`.** Node-definition `version` (and matching node-instance `typeVersion`) are validated by `versionSchema`, a regex that accepts both `x.y` and `x.y.z` (`/^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, error `'Version must be in format "x.y" or "x.y.z"'`). Both layers are canonically `x.y`, but the node-level regex still accepts legacy 3-part strings so registry definitions (`"1.0"`) and older scaffolded nodes (`"1.0.0"`) both parse. The two layers report distinct errors, but Zod may collapse a node-level mismatch to path `(root)`. If you see a version-related error at `(root)`, audit the top-level `version` first; if it's correct, check each node's `typeVersion` against the matching `definitions[].version`.

78	      "source": "=result.response",

85	      "var": "error"

91	**Required fields on every node**: `id`, `type`, `typeVersion`, **`display`** (with at least a `label`). This applies to **every** node — triggers (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers), action nodes, control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`), and human-task nodes. The Zod `nodeSchema` declares `display: displayConfigSchema` without `.optional()`, so no node type is exempt — even ones that "feel" trivial.
92	
93	`typeVersion` must match the corresponding `definitions[].version` exactly. The registry often returns versions such as `"1.0"` while older examples or scaffolded files may show `"1.0.0"`. If a node uses `typeVersion: "1.0.0"` but the copied definition is `"version": "1.0"`, validation reports "Node type `<type>:1.0.0` has no matching definition." When direct-authoring a new node from `registry get`, set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's `version`; when preserving an existing node, preserve its existing node/definition pair unless you intentionally update both together. <!-- version-check-skip --> (explains the x.y vs x.y.z mismatch mechanic; literals are illustrative, not pinned)
94	
95	> **Gotcha — vague schema-validation error on missing `display`.** Omitting `display` on any node produces:
96	>
97	> ```
98	> [error] [(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
99	> ```
100	>
101	> The error path is `(root)` and does NOT pinpoint which node or which field is missing. If you see this error after editing a `.flow` file, audit every node for a `display` block before doing anything else.
102	
103	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates all live in the node's **definition** (the manifest copied from the registry into `definitions[]`). The runtime hydrates them from the definition at serialization time — instances carry only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity onto each instance's `inputs.source`. Do not write a `"model": { "source": ... }` block on the instance.
104	>
105	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Position and size are stored in the top-level `layout` object, not on individual nodes. See [Layout](#layout) below.

135	### Node outputs
136	
137	`$vars.<sourceNodeId>.<outputId>` resolution at runtime is driven by **`variables.nodes[]`**, not by the node instance's `outputs` block. The BPMN emitter walks `variables.nodes[]` to write the process-level `<uipath:inputOutput id="<nodeId>.<outputId>">` declarations the runtime needs; the action-node instance `outputs` block is ignored at serialization (the manifest's `outputDefinition` supplies the activity-side mapping). End / terminate nodes are the exception — their instance `outputs` block IS consumed to map workflow-level `out` variables. See [end/impl.md](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md).
138	
139	The canonical recipe for a data-producing node is therefore:
140	
141	- `definitions[]` entry copied verbatim from `uip maestro flow registry get` (carries the manifest `outputDefinition`).
142	- `variables.nodes[]` entry per output: `{ "id": "<nodeId>.<outputId>", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "<nodeId>", "outputId": "<outputId>" } }`.
143	- Optional instance `outputs` block matching the manifest — harmless and matches the canonical examples below for clarity, but **not** what controls runtime variable visibility.
144	
145	Skipping `variables.nodes[]` produces a flow that passes `flow validate` but resolves `$vars.<sourceNodeId>.output` to `undefined` at runtime (MST-9972). `uip maestro flow format` regenerates `variables.nodes[]` from `nodes[]` + `definitions[]`, so always run it after structural edits — the omission becomes self-healing.
146	
147	When you DO author the instance `outputs` block (for documentation / parity with manifest schema), use the shape below. Each output entry has:
148	
149	- `type` — data type (usually `"object"`)
150	- `description` — human-readable description
151	- `source` — runtime binding expression (e.g., `"=result.response"` for the primary output, `"=result.Error"` for errors)
152	- `var` — the variable name (matches the output ID, e.g., `"output"`, `"error"`)
153	
154	The standard `outputs` block for most action nodes (script, HTTP, transform, connector, agent):
155	
156	```json
157	"outputs": {
158	  "output": {
159	    "type": "object",
160	    "description": "The return value of the <node type>",
161	    "source": "=result.response",
162	    "var": "output"
163	  },
164	  "error": {
165	    "type": "object",
166	    "description": "Error information if the <node type> fails",
167	    "source": "=result.Error",
168	    "var": "error"
169	  }
170	}
171	```
172	
173	Trigger nodes (manual, scheduled, connector triggers) have a single output — no error port:
174	
175	```json
176	"outputs": {
177	  "output": {
178	    "type": "object",
179	    "description": "The return value of the trigger.",
180	    "source": "=result.response",
181	    "var": "output"
182	  }
183	}
184	```
185	
186	End/terminate nodes do **not** use this pattern — their `outputs` maps workflow-level output variables (see the [Author end plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/end/impl.md)).

188	## Layout
189	
190	Node positioning is stored in a **top-level `layout` object**, keyed by node `id`. The same shape applies inside each subflow as `subflows[<id>].layout`. Layout data is owned by `uip maestro flow format` (see [cli-commands.md](cli-commands.md#uip-maestro-flow-format)) — you should not need to hand-write it.
191	
192	```json
193	"layout": {
194	  "nodes": {
195	    "start": {
196	      "position": { "x": 200, "y": 144 },
197	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
198	      "collapsed": false
199	    },
200	    "rollDice": {
201	      "position": { "x": 400, "y": 144 },
202	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
203	      "collapsed": false
204	    },
205	    "end": {
206	      "position": { "x": 600, "y": 144 },
207	      "size": { "width": 96, "height": 96 },
208	      "collapsed": false
209	    }
210	  }
211	}
212	```
213	
214	Each key in `layout.nodes` is a node `id`. `flow format` creates an entry for every node and populates `position` + `size`.
215	
216	**What format does:**
217	- Arranges nodes horizontally (left-to-right) with `nodeSpacing: 96`, anchored to the leftmost node's original position
218	- Sets each node's `size` to match its canvas shape: inline agents (`uipath.agent.autonomous` / `uipath.agent.conversational`, `shape: rectangle`) → `{ "width": 288, "height": 96 }`; containers (loops/groups) → `{ "width": 560, "height": 320 }`; everything else — including referenced `uipath.core.agent.<guid>` nodes — → `{ "width": 96, "height": 96 }`. A size that disagrees with the node's shape renders misshapen in Studio Web.
219	- Skips `stickyNote` nodes from layout (they keep their custom position and size)
220	- Recurses into every subflow and rewrites its `subflows[<id>].layout` map
221	
222	**Subflow layout is scoped.** Each subflow entry in `subflows[<id>]` has its **own** `layout.nodes` map for the nodes inside that subflow — they do NOT live in the top-level `layout.nodes`. Format handles both passes. See the [Author subflow plugin reference](../author/references/plugins/subflow/impl.md).

300	## Implicit error port on action nodes
301	
302	Any node with `supportsErrorHandling: true` in the registry exposes an implicit `error` source port for catching node-level failures. This applies to HTTP, Script, Transform (all variants), connector activities, agent nodes, and RPA nodes — essentially every action node.
303	
304	The port is **not** listed in the registry's `handleConfiguration`. Studio Web only exposes it when the source node has `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true`; when the flow contains an outgoing edge with `sourcePort: "error"` from that node, the serializer emits a BPMN boundary error event attached to the node. Because of this gate, `uip maestro flow validate` reports an error when a node has an outgoing `sourcePort: "error"` edge but `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled` is not `true` — so the inconsistency is caught before publish rather than surfacing as a hidden edge in Studio Web.
305	
306	### When the error port fires
307	
308	- Network failures, DNS errors, TLS errors
309	- Request timeouts
310	- Non-2xx HTTP responses (unless caught by a configured `inputs.branches` entry)
311	- Script exceptions (`throw`, undefined reference, etc.)
312	- Transform operation failures (invalid collection, missing field)
313	- Any unhandled runtime exception inside the node
314	
315	Without a wired error edge, any of these fails the whole flow with `finalStatus: "Faulted"`.
316	
317	### Wiring the error port
318	
319	```bash
320	# Confirm the node supports error handling
321	uip maestro flow registry get <node-type> --output json --output-filter "Node.SupportsErrorHandling"
322	
323	# Add an outgoing edge with sourcePort: "error"
324	uip maestro flow edge add <Project>.flow <actionNodeId> <errorHandlerId> \
325	  --source-port error --target-port input --output json
326	```
327	
328	`uip maestro flow edge add --source-port error` and `uip maestro flow format` set `inputs.errorHandlingEnabled: true` on the source node automatically. When editing `.flow` JSON directly, set the flag yourself:
329	
330	```json
331	{
332	  "id": "<actionNodeId>",
333	  "inputs": {
334	    "errorHandlingEnabled": true
335	  }
336	}
337	```
338	
339	Inside the error handler, `$vars.{actionNodeId}.error` resolves to the error object. For HTTP it's `{ code, message, detail, category, status }`; other nodes have similar shapes — check the node's `outputDefinition.error.schema` in the registry.
340	
341	### Error port vs other branching
342	
343	| Mechanism | When to use |
344	| --- | --- |
345	| **`error` source port** (any action node) | The node failed (exception, timeout, non-2xx not caught by a branch). Generic "something went wrong" handler. |
346	| **`branch-{id}` ports** (HTTP only, `inputs.branches`) | The call succeeded and you want to route on response *content* — different paths for e.g. empty vs non-empty results. |
347	| **`core.logic.decision` downstream** | Simple yes/no routing on the node's successful output. Doesn't help if the node itself fails. |
348	| **`core.logic.switch` downstream** | Multi-way routing on the node's successful output. Same — doesn't catch failures. |

467	## entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit
468	
469	`entry-points.json` declares the flow's external interface (input/output schemas and trigger entry points). **Do not edit this file directly** — it is auto-generated by `uip maestro flow init` and regenerated by `uip maestro flow debug` before upload. Manual edits will be overwritten.

471	Flow input and output parameters are declared through **variables** in the `.flow` file:
472	- **Flow inputs**: Add entries to `variables.nodes[]` whose `binding.nodeId` is the start node and whose `binding.outputId` names each input value — the start node "outputs" input values to downstream nodes
473	- **Flow outputs**: Add output variables to the end/terminate node
474	- Downstream nodes reference inputs via `$vars.start.output.<paramName>`
475	
476	The packaging/debug step derives `entry-points.json` from these variable declarations.

478	## Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)
479	
480	The top-level `bindings` array (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`, `variables`, `layout`) holds resource-reference indirections for **Orchestrator resource nodes** — RPA workflows, agents, flows, agentic processes, API workflows, and HITL apps.
481	
482	Each resource node needs two binding entries (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`). The node instance itself has no binding or context data — just `inputs`. The definition (copied verbatim from the registry) carries `model.context[]` templates like `<bindings.name>` and `<bindings.folderPath>`. At BPMN emit time the runtime rewrites those placeholders to `=bindings.<id>` by matching the placeholder name against a workflow-level binding, scoped by the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey`.
483	
484	```json
485	"bindings": [
486	  {
487	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID>",
488	    "name": "name",
489	    "type": "string",
490	    "resource": "process",
491	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
492	    "default": "<ResourceName>",
493	    "propertyAttribute": "name",
494	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
495	  },
496	  {
497	    "id": "<UNIQUE_ID_2>",
498	    "name": "folderPath",
499	    "type": "string",
500	    "resource": "process",
501	    "resourceKey": "<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>",
502	    "default": "<FolderPath>",
503	    "propertyAttribute": "folderPath",
504	    "resourceSubType": "Process"
505	  }
506	]
507	```
508	
509	**Rules:**
510	
511	- Add **two entries** per resource node (one for `name`, one for `folderPath`).
512	- **Share** entries across node instances that reference the same resource — do not duplicate. Matching is by `(resourceKey, name)`, so any node whose definition has the same `resourceKey` resolves to the same binding pair.
513	- Entry IDs are unique strings within the file. Descriptive IDs (e.g. `bDepositRpaName`) are preferred over short random IDs.
514	- The node instance has no `model` block — it carries only `inputs`, `outputs`, and `display`.
515	- `resourceKey` must exactly match the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` (verbatim from the registry). The runtime uses this key to scope placeholder resolution so that binding names like `name` / `folderPath` (shared across resource kinds) don't cross-alias.
516	- `resourceSubType` mirrors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceSubType`: `Process` (rpa), `Agent` (agent), `Flow` (flow), `ProcessOrchestration` (agentic-process), `Api` (api-workflow), or the app type for HITL.
517	
518	**Why this is required.** The definition's `model.context[].value` fields are placeholders of the form `<bindings.{name}>` — deliberately invalid as runtime expressions, so they can't be confused with one. Before the BPMN is emitted, the runtime rewrites each placeholder to `=bindings.<id>` by finding a workflow-level binding with `(resourceKey, name)` matching the node's manifest `model.bindings.resourceKey` + the placeholder name. Without matching entries in top-level `bindings[]`, `uip maestro flow debug` fails with "Folder does not exist or the user does not have access to the folder" even though `uip maestro flow validate` passes.
519	
520	**Definitions stay verbatim.** Do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the `definitions` entry — the definition is the authoring template. See "Every node type needs a `definitions` entry" in [author/CAPABILITY.md](../author/CAPABILITY.md).

524	**Not to be confused with `bindings_v2.json`.** That file holds connector connection bindings for Integration Service nodes — a separate system. A flow may have both: a top-level `bindings[]` for resource references and a `bindings_v2.json` file for connector connections.

1	# UiPath Solution Workspace
2	
3	> **A `.uipx` file in this directory marks a UiPath solution. Drive every solution operation through the `uip` CLI — packing, publishing, deploying, and deployment configuration.** Do not hand-edit `.uipx`; manage projects via `uip solution projects ...` so the manifest stays internally consistent.
4	
5	This file is a static snapshot, scaffolded by the `uip` CLI version `1.199.0-dev.7962`. If the CLI version you have access to is different, there may be inconsistencies in the commands or options listed below. When you encounter one, look up the current form with `uip <group> --help` and **edit this file in place** — find and replace the stale command with the working one.
6	
7	## The `.uipx` Manifest
8	
9	`<solution>.uipx` is a JSON document at the solution root listing every project in the solution. Skeleton:
10	
11	```json
12	{
13	    "DocVersion": "1.0.0",
14	    "StudioMinVersion": "2025.10.0",
15	    "SolutionId": "<uuid>",
16	    "Projects": [
17	        {
18	            "Type": "Process",
19	            "ProjectRelativePath": "MyProcess/project.json",
20	            "Id": "<uuid>"
21	        }
22	    ]
23	}
24	```
25	
26	Typical layout:
27	
28	```text
29	my-solution/
30	    my-solution.uipx          ← solution manifest
31	    AGENTS.md                 ← this file (Codex, Cursor, generic agents)
32	    CLAUDE.md                 ← identical copy (Claude Code)
33	    ProjectA/
34	        project.json
35	        bindings_v2.json      ← per-project resource declarations
36	        ...
37	    ProjectB/
38	        project.uiproj
39	        ...
40	```
41	
42	You must manage membership via the CLI, never by editing the manifest. All these operations work entirely on local files (`.uipx` plus the solution-builder artefacts on disk) and do not require `uip login` — auth is only needed once you reach `pack` / `publish` / `deploy` / `upload`.
43	
44	| Intent | Command |
45	|---|---|
46	| Create a solution | `uip solution init <name>` |
47	| Register an existing subfolder of the solution dir as a project (no copying — use after scaffolding *inside* the solution dir, e.g. `uip rpa create-project --location <solution-dir>`) | `uip solution projects add <project-path> [<solution-file>]` |
48	| Add a project from outside the solution — copies the folder at `<path>` into the solution dir and registers it (`<path>` is a local filesystem path) | `uip solution projects import <path>` |
49	| Unregister a project (does not delete the project files on disk) | `uip solution projects remove <project-path> [<solution-file>]` |
50	| List projects in the solution | `uip solution projects list` |
51	
52	The `uip ... init` scaffolders (`agent init`, `maestro flow init`, `maestro bpmn init`, `maestro case init`, `api-workflow init`) **auto-register** the new project when run inside a solution directory — they walk up for the enclosing `.uipx` and add it to `Projects[]` automatically, so a separate `project add` is not needed. Pass `--skip-solution-registration` to scaffold standalone without registering; the output's `Data.SolutionRegistration.Status` is then `OptedOut`. The full set of `Status` values is: `Registered` / `AlreadyRegistered` (added in this run / already present), `NotInSolution` (no enclosing `.uipx` found), `OptedOut` (`--skip-solution-registration` passed), `Skipped` (a candidate solution was found but registration was not safe to attempt — e.g. multiple `.uipx` in one directory, or the project sits outside the solution dir), and `Failed` (manifest read/parse/write error).
53	
54	## Project Types
55	
56	A solution can contain multiple projects of different types. The table below lists each project type and the `uip` command that scaffolds a fresh one (or marks the row when no scaffolding command exists).
57	
58	| Type | Description | Scaffold with | Skill |
59	|---|---|---|---|
60	| `Process` | RPA process — Studio workflow (XAML, Coded C#, or Hybrid) | `uip rpa create-project --name <name>` | `uipath-rpa` |
61	| `Library` | Reusable RPA library | `uip rpa create-project --template-id LibraryProcessTemplate --name <name>` | `uipath-rpa` |
62	| `Tests` | Test Automation project | `uip rpa create-project --template-id TestAutomationProjectTemplate --name <name>` | `uipath-rpa` |
63	| `Flow` | Maestro Flow — long-running orchestrated workflow | `uip maestro flow init <name>` | `uipath-maestro-flow` |
64	| `CaseManagement` | Maestro Case — stateful business process (SLA, approvals, HITL) | `uip maestro case init <name>` | `uipath-maestro-case` |
65	| `ProcessOrchestration` | Maestro BPMN — long-running orchestrated process | `uip maestro bpmn init <name>` | `uipath-maestro-bpmn` |
66	| `Agent` | LLM agent project — **low-code** (configured via `agent.json`; no Python) or **coded** (Python: LangGraph / LlamaIndex / OpenAI Agents). Both subtypes share `ProjectType: "Agent"`; the discriminator is `agent.json#type`. | `uip agent init <path>` (low-code) · `uip codedagent new [name]` (coded — see the `uipath-agents` skill for the full flow) | `uipath-agents` |
67	| `AppV2` | Coded App — web application | `uip codedapp init <path>` | `uipath-coded-apps` |
68	| `Function` | UiPath Function (JS / TS / Python) | `uip functions new [name]` | none |
69	| `Api` | API Workflow project | `uip api-workflow init <name>` | none |
70	| `Connector` | Integration Service connector | no CLI scaffolding — use `uip is connectors` to list / get / export existing connectors | none |
71	| `WebApp` | Legacy low-code UiPath App (the coded variant is `AppV2`) | no CLI scaffolding | none |
72	
73	All skill should be installed by running the command: `uip skills install`. The general-purpose `uipath-platform` skill covers what isn't in a type-specific skill.
74	
75	The type lives in either `project.uiproj` (top-level `ProjectType`) or `project.json` (`designOptions.outputType`, falling back to top-level `ProjectType` when `outputType` is absent — read or write either field). The `init` scaffolders above auto-register when run inside a solution directory (unless `--skip-solution-registration` is passed). For other scaffolders, register the project with the solution after scaffolding: use `uip solution projects add <project-path> [<solution-file>]` when the project already lives inside the solution directory (registers in place, no copy), or `uip solution projects import <path>` to copy a project from outside the solution dir into it and register it. If you pass an unknown type to those commands, they reject with the exhaustive accepted list — trust that error over this table.
76	
77	## End-to-End Lifecycle
78	
79	Run `uip login` first — most steps below need an authenticated session, including `solution pack` in some cases.
80	
81	```bash
82	# 1. Authenticate
83	#    Interactive (browser OAuth):
84	uip login
85	#    Non-interactive (CI / CD) with client credentials:
86	uip login --client-id <ID> --client-secret <SECRET> --tenant <TENANT>
87	
88	# 1a. (Optional) Restore project dependencies before packing. Resolves NuGet
89	#     deps (including authenticated Orchestrator feeds) so pack can compile.
90	#     Useful in CI: login -> restore -> pack. Takes <solutionPath> only; it
91	#     does not produce a package. Pack also restores internally, so this is an
92	#     optimization, not a requirement.
93	uip solution restore .
94	
95	# 2. Pack the solution into a .zip. Two positional args:
96	#    <solutionPath>  — solution dir (containing .uipx) or a .uis file
97	#    <output-path>   — directory where the .zip is written (required unless --dry-run)
98	uip solution pack . ./out
99	
100	# 2a. (Optional) Validate the solution against the strict deploy-time
101	#     pipeline without producing a package — useful as a CI gate.
102	uip solution pack . --dry-run
103	
104	# 3. Publish the packed .zip to Orchestrator
105	uip solution publish ./out/<package>.zip
106	
107	# 4. Fetch the default deployment configuration for the published package
108	uip solution deploy config get <package-name> --destination config.json
109	
110	# 5. (Optional) Customize the config — see "Deployment Configuration" below
111	
112	# 6. Deploy. By default this also activates; pass --skip-activate to defer.
113	uip solution deploy run \
114	    --name <deployment-name> \
115	    --package-name <package-name> \
116	    --package-version <version> \
117	    --folder-name <new-folder> \
118	    --parent-folder-path Shared \
119	    --config-file config.json
120	
121	# 7. The deploy returns a pipeline deployment ID — track it:
122	uip solution deploy status <pipeline-deployment-id>
123	
124	# 8. List every deployment in the active tenant
125	uip solution deploy list
126	```
127	
128	**Activation lifecycle.** `deploy run` activates by default. To split the steps:
129	
130	```bash
131	uip solution deploy run --skip-activate ...                      # leaves "Inactive (Ready to activate)"
132	uip solution deploy activate <deployment-name>     # activate later
133	uip solution deploy uninstall <deployment-name> --yes   # remove the deployment + its resources (--yes required; the CLI never prompts)
134	```
135	
136	`uninstall` and `activate` take the deployment name as a **positional** argument (no `--name` flag). `status` takes the **pipeline deployment ID** (the GUID returned by `deploy run`), also positional.
137	
138	## Package Signing
139	
140	`solution pack` can sign each packed project `.nupkg` with a code-signing certificate. Signing is opt-in: add `--signing-certificate-path <cert.pfx>` to the pack command. The certificate password (`--signing-certificate-password`) is optional — passing it as `env.VAR` (e.g. `env.SIGNING_PASSWORD`) is recommended, though an inline value also works. An optional timestamp server is set with `--signing-timestamp-server <url>`.
141	
142	## Studio Web (Browser Editing)
143	
144	Studio Web is a separate target from the Orchestrator deploy chain — it hosts a browser-based collaborative editor for solutions. The `solution upload` command pushes the local solution there and returns a `DesignerUrl` to open the solution in a browser; this is independent of `pack` / `publish` / `deploy` and does *not* produce a runtime-deployable artifact.
145	
146	```bash
147	uip solution upload .                      # upload solution dir to Studio Web as a new solution; returns DesignerUrl
148	uip solution upload . --force              # force-replace the existing Studio Web solution referenced by .uipx (destroys cloud version history)
149	uip solution download <solution-id>        # round-trip a Studio Web solution back to disk
150	uip solution delete <solution-id> --yes    # remove a solution from Studio Web (--yes required; the CLI never prompts)
151	```
152	
153	`upload` accepts a solution directory, a `.uipx` file, or a `.uis` file. It probes Studio Web for the bundled `SolutionId` first: if the cloud has no solution with that id, the upload imports as new; if a solution with that id already exists, the upload is refused unless `--force` is passed. Forcing replaces the cloud project in place and **wipes its Studio Web version history**, so use `--force` deliberately. To upload a copy as an unrelated cloud solution instead of overwriting, scaffold a fresh solution with `uip solution init` (or remove the `SolutionId` from the local `.uipx`) and re-run upload.
154	
155	## Per-Project Bindings (`bindings_v2.json`)
156	
157	Each project declares the resources it needs (assets, queues, buckets, processes, …) in a `bindings_v2.json` file at the project root. These declarations drive the solution's resource inventory.
158	
159	After editing a project's bindings, or after `solution projects import` (which doesn't auto-sync resources), reconcile the solution-level inventory:
160	
161	```bash
162	uip solution resources refresh     # re-scan every project, sync new / removed resources
163	```
164	
165	`solution resources refresh` creates new resources for bindings not yet in the solution and imports from Orchestrator when a matching resource already exists.
166	
167	Inspect the current solution inventory:
168	
169	```bash
170	uip solution resources list        # everything declared in this solution
171	```
172	
173	## Deployment Configuration
174	
175	The deploy config is a JSON file fetched from Orchestrator that lists every resource the solution will provision (or reuse) and every property you can override. It is **separate from `bindings_v2.json`** — bindings declare *what a project needs*, the deploy config decides *how that maps to Orchestrator at deploy time*.
176	
177	```bash
178	# Fetch the default config to a file
179	uip solution deploy config get <package-name> --destination config.json
180	
181	# Set a property on a single resource
182	uip solution deploy config set config.json <resource-name> <property> <value>
183	# e.g. set config.json MyQueue maxNumberOfRetries 5
184	
185	# Set a property on every resource (limited; supports e.g. conflictFixingAction)
186	uip solution deploy config set config.json --all <property> <value>
187	
188	# Link a resource slot to an existing Orchestrator resource (instead of creating a new one)
189	uip solution deploy config link config.json <resource-name> \
190	    --name <existing-resource-name> \
191	    --folder-path Shared/Production
192	
193	# Remove a link — the resource will be created at deploy time again
194	uip solution deploy config unlink config.json <resource-name>
195	
196	# Apply the customized config:
197	uip solution deploy run ... --config-file config.json
198	```
199	
200	If a deploy fails on a configuration issue, the CLI prints the offending resource and an `Instructions` field. Read those before retrying — most failures are an `existing-resource-name` typo, a wrong `--folder-path`, or a property that the resource type does not accept.
201	
202	## Resource Types in Orchestrator
203	
204	The CLI talks about the same resource types Orchestrator does:
205	
206	- **Assets** — key-value configuration. Asset value types: `Text`, `Bool`, `Integer`, `Credential`, `Secret`.
207	- **Queues** & **Queue Items** — work-item queues for distributed transactional processing; queue items are the rows.
208	- **Storage Buckets** & **Bucket Files** — file storage for automation data.
209	- **Connections** — Integration Service connections to external systems (Salesforce, ServiceNow, …).
210	- **Processes / Releases** — published packages bound to a folder.
211	- **Triggers** & **Webhooks** — event-, time-, or queue-based job firing; outbound HTTP notifications.
212	- **Entities** — Data Service tables. Add or bind with kind `Entity`.
213	- **ChoiceSets** — enumerations used by entity fields. Add with kind `ChoiceSet`.
214	
215	Resources outside a solution are managed under the orchestrator tool, which exposes per-type subgroups (`uip or assets …`, `uip or queues …`, `uip or buckets …`, `uip or bucket-files …`, `uip or libraries …`, `uip or queue-items …`, `uip or triggers …`, `uip or webhooks …`). Run `uip or --help` for the live list. Example:
216	
217	```bash
218	uip or assets list          # list assets in the active folder
219	uip or assets create        # create an asset (see --help)
220	```
221	
222	## Output Conventions for Agents
223	
224	Two rules make automation reliable:
225	
226	1. **Never redirect or drop stderr.** Errors and confirmations go to stderr — `2>/dev/null` will silently hide failures and produce false retries.
227	2. **Use `--output-filter <jmespath>`** to extract specific fields rather than piping JSON through external tools. The expression is applied to the `Data` array — start with `[]`, not with `Data[]`. Example: `uip solution packages list --output-filter "[].name"`.
228	
229	Standard success shape: `{ "Result": "Success", "Code": "<CommandCode>", "Data": ... }`.
230	Standard failure shape: `{ "Result": "Failure", "Message": "<short>", "Instructions": "<actionable>" }`.
231	
232	List commands always return `Data: []` on empty results — never a message object — so consumers can rely on a consistent array shape.
233	
234	## Discovering Commands
235	
236	This file is a starting map, not a reference. The live source of truth is the CLI itself:
237	
238	```bash
239	uip --help                       # top-level groups
240	uip solution --help              # every solution verb
241	uip solution deploy --help       # the deploy subgroup
242	uip <command> --help             # full options for any command
243	```
244	
245	For concept or API documentation beyond CLI usage, fetch `https://docs.uipath.com/llms.txt` for the product index, then the relevant `.md` page (e.g. `https://docs.uipath.com/orchestrator/automation-cloud/latest/api-guide/assets-requests.md`).
246	
247	Adjacent groups commonly used alongside solutions:
248	
249	| Group | Purpose |
250	|---|---|
251	| `uip login`, `uip login tenant` | Authenticate, switch tenants |
252	| `uip or folders` | Manage Orchestrator folders |
253	| `uip or assets`, `uip or queues`, `uip or buckets`, `uip or bucket-files`, `uip or libraries`, `uip or queue-items`, `uip or triggers`, `uip or webhooks` | Manage Orchestrator resources directly |
254	| `uip rpa` | RPA workflow lifecycle (compile, validate, execute, scaffold) |
255	| `uip maestro` | Maestro Flow / Case / BPMN scaffolding |
256	| `uip agent`, `uip codedagent` | Coded agent lifecycle |
257	| `uip codedapp` | Coded Apps lifecycle |
258	| `uip functions` | UiPath Functions |
259	| `uip tm` | Test Manager (test projects, sets, executions) |
260	| `uip is` | Integration Service (connectors, connections) |
261	| `uip tools` | Manage CLI tool extensions |
262	
263	## Troubleshooting Quick Map
264	
265	| Symptom | First thing to check |
266	|---|---|
267	| `Not authenticated` / 401 | `uip login`, then re-run |
268	| Command targets the wrong tenant | `uip login tenant set <tenant>`; verify with `uip login status` |
269	| Pack succeeds but publish 409s | Version conflict — bump the version (`uip solution pack . ./out -v <new-version>`) or delete the colliding version with `uip solution packages delete <package-name> <version> --yes` (only if intentional; `--yes` required) |
270	| `deploy run` fails on a resource conflict | `uip solution deploy config link config.json <resource> --name <existing> --folder-path <path>` to map to the existing one, or change `conflictFixingAction` via `config set` |
271	| `Resource not found` after deploy | `uip solution resources refresh` to re-sync from each project's `bindings_v2.json`; if still missing, the resource was never declared in any project |
272	| Output looks empty | You may have redirected stderr — confirmations and errors go there. Re-run without `2>` |
273	
274	---
